description: CV expander for CHAN-IN, giving voltage control of its gain, its two filters and its phase invert

params.text: Attenuverter on the gain CV, -100% to +100%, and at 0% when the module is added
Attenuverter on the high cut CV, -100% to +100%, and at 0% when the module is added
Attenuverter on the low cut CV, -100% to +100%, and at 0% when the module is added

inputs.text: Shifts the gain on CHAN-IN, ±10V covering the whole -60dB to +6dB range with the attenuverter fully open, added to the GAIN knob and clamped to that range
Sets the high cut frequency on CHAN-IN at 1V per octave from 4472Hz, the middle of its range; it replaces the HPF knob rather than adding to it, and the result is clamped to 1kHz to 20kHz
Sets the low cut frequency on CHAN-IN at 1V per octave from 100Hz, the middle of its range; it replaces the LPF knob rather than adding to it, and the result is clamped to 20Hz to 500Hz
Inverts the phase on CHAN-IN whenever the voltage here is above 1V, whatever the PHASE button is set to

notes: The module does nothing unless CHAN-IN is immediately to its left.
Every attenuverter is at 0% when the module is added, so the gain, HPF and LPF jacks do nothing until one is turned up.
Turning an attenuverter on the HPF or LPF jack takes that filter's knob on CHAN-IN out of use, and the frequency is then set by the patched voltage alone.
The dots either side of the X in the title fade from white to amber once CHAN-IN is found on the left.

inputs.0:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.2: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.3:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
